# Canvas Assignment Bodies, Paste-Ready

**Generated by `scripts/build-canvas-events.js`. Do not hand-edit.**

One assignment per topic, the graded companion to the calendar event in
`calendar-events.md`. Both are generated from the same schedule and the same
lesson data by the same code, so the two Canvas objects for a topic cannot
disagree about its targets, its criteria, its dates, or its required work.

```bash
node scripts/build-canvas-events.js          # write
node scripts/build-canvas-events.js --check  # fail on drift, write nothing
```

## The required module list

**A topic runs ten module cards and its assignment collects a subset.** Topic
1.5 requires six, 1.6 requires five. Which ones is a teaching decision, so it
is not derived from anything: it is the `modules` field on that topic's days in
`assets/data/announcements-schedule.js`, read off the Required Work row of the
assignment as it stands in Canvas today.

That is the **same field the announcements board reads** for its "Today's
Required Modules" slide. One field, two surfaces, so the wall and Canvas cannot
name different work. A topic with no list is not printed below; it is listed as
pending instead, because an assignment that asked for all ten when the real one
asks for six is worse than no assignment at all.

Every module the topic runs but does not require prints under its own
**Optional Support / Go Deeper** row instead, by number and name, with language
that says the work is available rather than quietly expected. A topic that
requires everything it runs prints no Optional Support row at all.

Each module's one-line description, required or optional, comes from the
lesson data wherever the lesson data has one, a checkpoint's `cardDesc`, the
reading's title, the Skill Builder's. Where the Canvas wording differs from the
card wording, it is authored in `MODULE_NOTES` in the builder, the same way
OVERVIEWS is. An optional module missing a description prints its bare name
rather than warning, since only a required module with no instructions is a
defect.

## How to paste one of these

1. Canvas, Assignments, the assignment for this topic, **Edit**.
2. In the Rich Content Editor, click the **`</>`** icon to open the HTML editor.
   **Never paste this into the visual editor.** Pasting rendered HTML there
   injects wrapper `<div>`s and inline font declarations that collapse the table.
3. Paste the whole block, the masthead `<div>` and the `<table>` together.
4. In **Assign to**, add one row per section using the table printed with the
   assignment, and remove the Everyone row so no student inherits the wrong date.
5. Save.

**The assignment name is not generated.** It has to be identical in Canvas and
PowerSchool, character for character, and ASCII only. See Section 2 of
`CANVAS-BUILD-GUIDE.md`; the topic code and full title are printed with each
block so the short name can be written from them, not guessed at here.
